artworks.title: Poseidon of Melos
artworks.description: Hellenistic marble statue of Poseidon found on the island of Melos, now in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens. The sea god stands in a commanding pose, his raised right hand once gripping a trident, with a dolphin at his feet supporting the figure.

artworks.title: Neptune and Triton
artworks.description: Early marble group by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, carved to crown a garden fountain in Rome and now in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London. Neptune thrusts his trident downward to command the waters while the young Triton crouches between his legs, blowing a conch shell.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Harryhausen's sea god looses the Kraken at Zeus' command — Poseidon as the hand that opens the deep, even when the thunderbolt gives the order.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps Poseidon as Odysseus' implacable enemy: the blinded Cyclops' father who will not forgive, and will not let the sea go still.

films.title: Immortals
films.description: Tarsem's pantheon brings Poseidon into the melee against the Titans — trident and seafoam in a fight choreographed like a Renaissance fresco come loose.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Poseidon's boons in Supergiant's roguelike are all knockback and surf — the earth-shaker as a splash of force that clears a room.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's demigod series makes Poseidon the absent father of its hero: the sea god's claim on Percy is the secret that opens Camp Half-Blood and a generation's gateway into Greek myth.
